title: Bmg Pays Tribute To Rochelle Fleming
text:
Bmg Pays Tribute To Rochelle Fleming | BMG 
 Combined Company Publishing Recordings Sync & Licensing Who We Are Careers News Tools Contact MENU BMG Pays Tribute to Rochelle Fleming 
 NOVEMBER 9, 2026
 Rochelle Fleming
 We are deeply saddened by the passing of Rochelle Fleming, the beloved founding member and lead singer of First Choice, whose extraordinary voice helped shape Philadelphia soul and disco and left a lasting mark on dance music. 
 A Philadelphia native, Fleming began singing with school friends in the group that would become First Choice. Their breakthrough came in 1973 with “Armed and Extremely Dangerous”, followed by “Smarty Pants” and “The Player”. Her powerful, expressive vocals gave the group’s recordings their unmistakable character. 
 Working with producer Norman Harris, First Choice went on to record for Gold Mind, a label associated with Salsoul. Their 1977 album Delusions featured “Doctor Love” and “Let No Man Put Asunder”, while later recordings included “Love Thang” and “Double Cross”. Together, these songs helped bridge the worlds of Philadelphia soul, disco and the emerging sound of house music. 
 “Let No Man Put Asunder” became particularly influential, embraced by generations of DJs and producers through remixes, samples and reinterpretations. 
 BMG represents part of First Choice’s catalog through Salsoul, helping preserve recordings that remain part of dance music culture today. 
 Dan Baxter, SVP, Global Catalog Recordings, BMG, said: “Rochelle was a remarkable singer, and the records she made with First Choice have had a lasting influence on dance music. “Doctor Love”, “Love Thang” and “Let No Man Put Asunder” still connect with dancers and DJs around the world, while remixes and samples have introduced her voice to successive generations. Our heartfelt condolences go to Rochelle’s family, friends and fellow members of First Choice. Her voice and the joy it brought to so many will not be forgotten.”
